items.question:
A tax associate is evaluating two tasks for Claude assistance. Task 1: converting 500 expense receipts per month from PDF to a structured expense table. Task 2: advising a client on whether a cross-border acquisition triggers transfer pricing obligations under a specific bilateral tax treaty.

Which TWO statements about these tasks are correct? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Task 1 is high-fit because it is high-volume, repetitive, and has a well-defined correct output structure.
options.B: Task 1 is poor-fit because Claude cannot read PDF documents.
options.C: Task 2 is poor-fit for unsupervised AI assistance because it requires current, jurisdiction-specific treaty interpretation.
options.D: Task 2 is high-fit because it is a complex reasoning task where a higher-tier model excels.
options.E: Both tasks require the same level of human oversight before output is used.

items.question:
An operations analyst at a retail chain receives weekly sales data from 200 store locations in varied CSV formats. Before analysis can begin, each file must be reorganised into a standard nine-column reporting template.

Which aspect of this task is MOST suitable for Claude to assist with?

options.A: Transforming each store's raw CSV into the standard reporting template format.
options.B: Deciding which underperforming stores should have staffing levels reduced.
options.C: Setting the performance benchmarks included in the standard reporting template.
options.D: Sending each store manager their individual performance summary automatically.

items.question:
A paralegal at a law firm receives 80 new client intake forms per week and must extract four fields from each — client name, case type, opposing counsel, and jurisdiction — before entering them into the case management system.

Which characteristic of this task makes it MOST suitable for Claude assistance?

options.A: The extracted data will be entered into the firm's case management system downstream.
options.B: The law firm employs a large number of attorneys who will use the extracted data.
options.C: The intake forms are received from courts across multiple jurisdictions.
options.D: The same four fields must be extracted from every form using the same consistent definitions.

items.question:
A social services agency proposes having Claude conduct initial crisis screening conversations with at-risk individuals who contact the helpline after hours, and automatically decide whether to escalate to on-call staff.

What is the PRIMARY reason this should NOT be automated as described?

options.A: After-hours call volume is typically too low to justify investment in an AI-driven screening workflow.
options.B: Claude cannot access the agency's case management records in real time without a custom integration.
options.C: Crisis screening requires empathetic human engagement and clinical risk judgement; an error in escalation decisions can directly harm a vulnerable individual.
options.D: A simpler automated triage algorithm based on keyword detection would handle the escalation decision more reliably than Claude.

items.question:
A finance operations associate must categorise 3,000 expense line items per month against a 20-category chart of accounts. The categorisation rules are fully documented in a 4-page policy that the team follows consistently.

Why is this a HIGH-fit task for Claude assistance?

options.A: Three thousand line items is the recognised minimum volume that justifies AI involvement in finance operations.
options.B: The task applies a fully documented ruleset consistently across a large number of similar inputs.
options.C: Expense categorisation is a domain in which Claude has specialist accounting expertise.
options.D: Finance tasks are generally better suited to AI than tasks in other business domains.

items.question: A media company's content operations team is evaluating which tasks to automate with Claude. Which TWO characteristics most strongly indicate a task is APPROPRIATE for Claude-assisted automation? (Choose TWO)

options.A: The task produces a structured output format that can be validated against a defined template or specification.
options.B: The task has never been performed before and requires developing the process as it runs.
options.C: The task involves applying the same transformation or extraction logic to many instances.
options.D: The task requires deep understanding of the company's five-year content strategy.
options.E: The task involves making final editorial decisions on which content gets published.

items.question:
An HR coordinator is designing a new-employee onboarding workflow. The steps are: (1) collect personal details from the new hire, (2) generate the employment contract draft from the standard template, (3) send the draft to legal for review, (4) issue the finalised signed contract.

Which step is MOST clearly suited for Claude to assist with?

options.A: Collecting personal details directly from the new hire in a real-time conversation.
options.B: Reviewing the contract draft on behalf of the legal team.
options.C: Deciding whether the new hire is eligible to start on the proposed date.
options.D: Generating the contract draft by populating the standard template with the new hire's details.

items.question:
A management consultant is helping a client analyse 40 customer interview transcripts for a journey-mapping project. Each transcript is 15–20 pages of unscripted responses. The thematic framework has been agreed in advance.

How should this work be classified and what workflow design follows?

options.A: Batch work; Claude processes all 40 transcripts against the defined thematic framework, and the consultant synthesises and validates the theme output across the full set.
options.B: Interactive work; the consultant must approve each transcript's themes before Claude processes the next one to avoid compounding errors.
options.C: Interactive work; theme identification from unscripted interviews requires real-time dialogue between Claude and the consultant for each transcript.
options.D: Batch work; Claude should produce the final journey map without human synthesis because the volume exceeds practical manual review capacity.

items.question:
A product manager's sprint release-notes workflow is: (1) engineering team submits ticket summaries, (2) Claude drafts customer-facing release notes from the summaries, (3) engineering lead verifies technical accuracy, (4) notes are published.

A new team member suggests reversing steps 1 and 2 — having Claude draft from tickets first, then collecting engineer summaries to validate. What is the BEST argument for keeping the ORIGINAL sequence?

options.A: Engineers are more motivated to write thorough summaries when they know release notes have already been drafted from their tickets.
options.B: Claude produces more accurate release notes when it has the ticket summaries in context before drafting begins.
options.C: Collecting complete inputs before drafting avoids producing release notes that must be revised when engineer summaries reveal information not in the raw tickets.
options.D: The engineering lead's verification step in step 3 becomes unnecessary if Claude drafts directly from tickets without summaries.

items.question:
A customer success manager at a B2B software company proposes having Claude send personalised renewal outreach messages to 50 at-risk accounts, tailored using each account's usage data, with no CSM review before delivery.

What is the MOST significant concern with this design?

options.A: Claude cannot analyse product usage data without a custom API integration to the product database.
options.B: Renewal outreach for at-risk accounts requires relationship judgement that varies per account; unreviewed automated messages may damage the relationship rather than protect it.
options.C: Fifty accounts is too small a volume to justify automated outreach over individual CSM outreach.
options.D: Personalisation based on usage data raises data privacy concerns that make this workflow inappropriate.

items.question:
A quality control engineer at a pharmaceutical manufacturer is redesigning the batch release documentation workflow. Steps include: extracting numerical test results from standardised lab reports, comparing results to documented specification limits, drafting the batch release summary, and the QC director signing the batch release certificate.

Which step should DEFINITELY remain a human step?

options.A: Extracting numerical test results from standardised lab report PDFs.
options.B: Comparing extracted results to the documented specification limits.
options.C: Drafting the batch release summary from the comparison results.
options.D: Signing the batch release certificate as the authorised quality decision.

items.question:
A marketing analyst has built a workflow to summarise weekly campaign performance reports. She defined a summary template and five KPIs to extract, and has validated the prompt on last week's single report. She now wants to expand the workflow to process all 12 regional reports simultaneously each week.

What should she do NEXT before expanding to all 12 regions?

options.A: Run the prompt across a sample of historical reports from different regions to confirm it handles regional format variations before committing to the full weekly run.
options.B: Publish the prompt to the wider analytics team so all members can replicate the workflow immediately.
options.C: Switch to batch API processing to handle 12 simultaneous reports efficiently at scale.
options.D: Increase the prompt's output length constraints to ensure all regional KPI variations are captured.

items.question: A corporate legal department is mapping its inbound contract review process to identify Claude-assisted steps. Which TWO steps are MOST appropriate for Claude assistance? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Determining which contracts require regulatory approval before execution.
options.B: Identifying and listing key obligations, deadlines, and payment terms in each submitted contract.
options.C: Providing the legal opinion that confirms the contract is compliant and safe to execute.
options.D: Flagging contract clauses that deviate from the company's standard approved terms.
options.E: Signing the contract on behalf of the company's general counsel.

items.question:
A research librarian at a university needs Claude to produce one-paragraph summaries of 400 academic papers for a literature database. All 400 papers are already available as PDFs. She wants to verify summary quality before the summaries go into the database.

What is the BEST workflow design for this task?

options.A: Have Claude summarise all 400 papers and publish them directly without sampling to avoid delays in the database going live.
options.B: Have Claude summarise one paper at a time, with the librarian reviewing each before requesting the next, to ensure quality throughout.
options.C: Run Claude on a pilot batch of 20 papers, review quality and adjust the prompt if needed, then process the remaining 380 with periodic spot-checks.
options.D: Use a higher-tier model for the entire 400-paper run to maximise summary quality and eliminate the need for human review.

items.question:
A property insurance claims adjuster proposes using Claude to analyse each claim's narrative, policy document, and field notes, then recommend approve, deny, or request-more-information for 200 water damage claims per month. The workflow would allow a manager to review a 10% random sample but route all other recommendations directly to action.

A compliance lead objects. What is the MOST precise statement of the concern?

options.A: Claude lacks the domain expertise to interpret insurance policy language accurately.
options.B: Routing 90% of claims decisions directly to action without review removes licensed adjuster accountability from determinations that are legally and regulatorily required to rest with a qualified professional.
options.C: Two hundred claims per month is insufficient volume to justify the implementation cost of AI-assisted claims processing.
options.D: Field notes are unstructured text that Claude cannot reliably process for claims analysis.

items.question:
A talent acquisition lead designs an AI-assisted hiring workflow: (1) Claude screens resumes against 8 defined criteria and shortlists candidates, (2) shortlisted candidates are auto-invited to a video interview, (3) Claude analyses interview transcripts and issues a hire/no-hire recommendation, (4) a recruiter reviews the recommendation and makes the final call.

Legal counsel identifies one step as most likely to attract employment discrimination scrutiny. Which step is it?

options.A: Claude screening resumes against 8 defined criteria to produce a shortlist.
options.B: The automated video interview invitation sent to shortlisted candidates.
options.C: The recruiter reviewing Claude's recommendation and making the final hiring decision.
options.D: Claude analysing interview transcripts to produce a hire/no-hire recommendation on an individual candidate.

items.question: A data team lead is designing a Claude-assisted analytics reporting workflow for an energy company. Which THREE design decisions reflect sound workflow principles? (Choose THREE)

options.A: Running a sample of 10 reports manually in parallel with Claude's outputs during the first month to establish a quality baseline.
options.B: Removing the analyst review step once Claude's accuracy exceeds 95% on the initial test set.
options.C: Keeping the CFO's sign-off step on the monthly board report as a human step regardless of Claude's performance.
options.D: Having Claude produce the strategic interpretation of energy market trends for the board presentation without senior analyst review.
options.E: Defining explicit acceptance criteria for each report type before the workflow goes live.

items.question: A business team is evaluating which tasks to automate with Claude. Which TWO characteristics most strongly indicate a task is a POOR fit for autonomous Claude processing? (Choose TWO)

options.A: The task involves reading a large volume of documents across multiple formats.
options.B: The task output is irreversible once delivered to an external party, and errors cannot be corrected after the fact.
options.C: The task requires processing data that arrives in varied or inconsistent formats.
options.D: The task requires a licensed professional to personally exercise and attest to professional judgement for each output.
options.E: The task has not previously been formally documented as a written process.

items.question:
A compliance officer builds a GDPR contract review workflow: (1) Claude reviews all 300 vendor contracts and flags those with potential compliance issues, (2) a legal associate reviews only the flagged contracts in detail, (3) remediation is applied to flagged contracts.

A risk manager warns the design has a systematic flaw. What is the flaw?

options.A: Contracts that Claude does not flag are assumed compliant and receive no human review, creating undetected miss risk if Claude's flagging is imperfect.
options.B: 300 contracts is too large a volume for a single-pass Claude review without chunking the analysis into smaller groups.
options.C: Legal associates should review all 300 contracts because AI-assisted contract review has no recognised value in compliance workflows.
options.D: The compliance officer, not a legal associate, should review flagged contracts to maintain role accountability.

items.question:
A customer experience team at a retail bank deploys Claude to respond to thousands of customer complaint emails per day. An engineer notices that Claude declines to respond to a subset of messages that contain aggressive or threatening language, flagging them rather than drafting a reply.

What should the workflow design specify for these flagged cases?

options.A: Retry the same prompt with a softer instruction set to encourage Claude to produce a draft despite the difficult content.
options.B: Discard the flagged messages from the queue and process only the cases Claude can handle.
options.C: Route flagged messages to a specialist human team trained in managing escalated or sensitive customer complaints.
options.D: Store the flagged messages and process them as a batch at the end of the day when queue pressure is lower.

items.question:
A procurement manager at a manufacturing plant uses Claude to generate supplier payment recommendations based on invoice data and payment terms. A colleague proposes connecting Claude's output directly to the payment processing system so approved amounts are released automatically.

What is the PRIMARY risk of this design?

options.A: Claude may calculate payment amounts in a currency format that is incompatible with the payment processing system.
options.B: The payment processing system may not support the data structure Claude produces without a validated integration layer.
options.C: AI-generated payment amounts would reach the payment system without a human verifying each transaction, creating STP on financial outflows.
options.D: Suppliers may object to receiving payments calculated by an AI system without human authorisation.

items.question:
A clinical documentation specialist at a hospital uses Claude to extract structured diagnosis codes from free-text physician notes. Occasionally Claude produces outputs where multiple code options are listed rather than a single code, indicating ambiguity in the source note.

What should the workflow design specify for these ambiguous outputs?

options.A: Default to the first code Claude lists, as its ordering reflects confidence ranking.
options.B: Instruct Claude to always select one code by adding 'choose the most likely option' to the prompt, eliminating ambiguous outputs.
options.C: Route ambiguous outputs to a certified clinical coder for manual code selection, treating Claude's multiple options as candidates rather than a final classification.
options.D: Exclude ambiguous outputs from the coding run and return them to the ordering physician to rewrite the note with more diagnostic clarity.

items.question:
A managing director at a logistics company has mandated that all outbound freight quotes be processed through a Claude-assisted pricing workflow. During a 4-hour Claude service outage on a Tuesday morning, the sales team cannot issue any quotes and loses three time-sensitive bids.

What is the MOST appropriate corrective action for the workflow design?

options.A: Implement a secondary AI pricing tool as a hot standby that activates automatically when Claude is unavailable.
options.B: Document and train a manual pricing procedure that sales staff can execute independently during Claude outages, and define the trigger conditions that activate it.
options.C: Negotiate an uptime SLA with Anthropic that compensates the company for bids lost during service outages.
options.D: Build a cache of recent Claude-generated pricing outputs that the sales team can reference during outages for similar bid types.

items.question:
A patient services coordinator at a speciality clinic uses Claude to draft patient intake summaries from structured intake forms. The coordinator reviews each summary and, when satisfied, copies the content into the clinic's electronic health record (EHR). The clinic director wants to replace the copy-paste step with an automated EHR write triggered when the coordinator clicks 'Approve'.

What must be confirmed before implementing this change?

options.A: The EHR system supports an API endpoint for receiving externally generated clinical notes in the clinic's configured note format.
options.B: The coordinator's 'Approve' action constitutes a legally valid clinical attestation for EHR entries under applicable healthcare record regulations.
options.C: Claude's intake summary will always match the character limit of the EHR note field to avoid truncation on write.
options.D: The automated write will not overwrite previous notes already present in the patient's EHR record.

items.question:
A digital ops manager at an insurance company automates a policy-renewal workflow: Claude reads structured policy data, generates a renewal letter, and the system emails it directly to the policyholder. No human step is included. After two months, the manager discovers that renewal letters for policies with mid-term endorsements reflect the original policy terms rather than the endorsed terms, because the structured data feed did not include endorsement records.

What does this incident MOST directly illustrate?

options.A: Claude cannot reliably process insurance policy data without domain-specific fine-tuning.
options.B: Removing the human review step eliminated the control that would have caught data completeness errors before they reached policyholders.
options.C: The email delivery system should have held renewal letters in a queue for at least 24 hours to allow error detection.
options.D: The structured data feed should have been validated by the IT team before the workflow went live.

items.question:
A business systems analyst at a 2,000-person logistics company is configuring a Claude connector to the company's order management system (OMS). The use case is helping customer service agents quickly summarise order status for customers. A developer suggests also enabling write access so Claude can update order records directly when customers request changes.

What is the MOST important design consideration before enabling write access?

options.A: Whether write operations to the OMS will increase API call volume enough to affect system performance.
options.B: Whether Claude's write actions will be logged with the specific change made, the customer interaction that triggered it, and the agent who was present during the session.
options.C: Whether the OMS supports rollback functionality for records updated through the API in case of erroneous writes.
options.D: Whether customers have consented to having their order records updated by an AI system rather than a human agent.

items.question:
A paralegal at a 15-attorney law firm uses Claude to process 200 lease agreements per month, extracting key terms into a structured data table. The managing partner wants to add a review checkpoint. The paralegal proposes reviewing every extracted record. The partner's preference is to review only the final data table once all 200 leases are processed.

Which approach is MOST appropriate for this use case?

options.A: The paralegal's approach: review each extracted record as it is produced to catch errors early, before they accumulate.
options.B: The partner's approach: review the complete 200-record table once processing is finished, which is more efficient.
options.C: Neither: apply a risk-stratified sampling approach that reviews 100% of leases above a defined value threshold and samples the remainder.
options.D: Neither: process a sample batch of 20 leases first, review those thoroughly, and use findings to adjust the extraction prompt before processing the remaining 180.

items.question:
A sanctions compliance analyst at a bank uses Claude to screen transaction counterparties. Claude identifies a counterparty name that is an 85% fuzzy match to a sanctioned entity on the SDN list but rates its own confidence as 'uncertain.' Under the bank's current workflow, uncertain matches are auto-cleared if no senior analyst reviews them within 24 hours. The compliance director is reviewing this design.

Which assessment is MOST accurate?

options.A: The 24-hour review window is reasonable because it balances operational efficiency with the need for human oversight of uncertain matches.
options.B: The auto-clear on inaction creates an opt-out oversight mechanism for a potential sanctions match — the bank cannot demonstrate active human clearance of cases that time out.
options.C: The design is adequate provided the bank can document that senior analysts are expected to review uncertain matches within the 24-hour window.
options.D: The design is acceptable because an 85% fuzzy match is below the threshold that constitutes a probable sanctions hit requiring mandatory human review.

items.question:
A senior underwriter at a specialty insurer uses two different Claude-assisted tools: Tool A analyses structured risk data from the application form; Tool B analyses unstructured broker correspondence. On a complex D&O application, Tool A recommends a moderate risk band; Tool B flags several concerning statements in broker emails that suggest the applicant may have undisclosed claims history. The underwriter must produce a binding quote within 4 hours.

What is the MOST appropriate NEXT step for the underwriter?

options.A: Average the outputs from Tool A and Tool B and produce a quote at the midpoint risk band, reflecting both data sources.
options.B: Use Tool A's output as the primary signal, since structured risk data is more reliable than unstructured correspondence analysis.
options.C: Treat the conflicting outputs as an escalation signal and contact the broker directly to clarify the correspondence before binding.
options.D: Apply a conservative loading to the Tool A risk band to account for the uncertainty flagged by Tool B, and bind at that loaded rate within the deadline.

items.question:
A head of compliance at a consumer lender reviews the audit trail for a Claude-assisted credit decision workflow. The trail records: the applicant's data file, the Claude-generated credit assessment, and the final credit decision (approved/declined). The compliance officer notes that the log does not capture which version of the credit model prompt was active when each assessment was run, nor whether the prompt was modified between assessments.

Why is this a significant audit trail gap?

options.A: Without the prompt version, the lender cannot reproduce the exact Claude output for a given applicant if challenged — two different prompts on the same data could produce different credit assessments.
options.B: The prompt version is legally required under consumer credit regulations and its absence constitutes a regulatory violation.
options.C: Recording prompt versions is primarily a software development concern and belongs in the IT change log, not the credit decision audit trail.
options.D: Without the prompt version, the lender cannot benchmark Claude's performance against competitor models under the same conditions.

items.question: An actuarial director at a large reinsurance company is designing a three-stage Claude-assisted pipeline for treaty pricing: Stage 1 — Claude extracts loss statistics from cedant data files; Stage 2 — Claude models expected loss ratios using the extracted statistics; Stage 3 — Claude generates a pricing recommendation. The director must decide where to place human-in-the-loop checkpoints. Which TWO placements are MOST important? (Choose TWO)

options.A: A checkpoint after Stage 1 to verify that loss statistics were extracted correctly before they propagate into the modelling and pricing stages.
options.B: A checkpoint within Stage 2 to review each individual modelling assumption as Claude applies it.
options.C: A checkpoint after Stage 3 to review and approve the pricing recommendation before it is communicated to the cedant.
options.D: A checkpoint before Stage 1 to confirm that the cedant data file has been classified as an authorised data source.
options.E: A checkpoint during Stage 2 to ensure the modelling method selected by Claude is appropriate for this cedant's loss history pattern.

items.question: A systems architect at a healthcare network is reviewing a Claude connector to the patient relationship management (PRM) system. The connector was originally scoped for read-only access to support patient communication drafting. A product manager requests expanding it to allow Claude to update appointment records, flag accounts for follow-up, and add notes to patient files — all triggered by conversation context without explicit agent approval. Which TWO design controls are MOST critical before enabling these write capabilities? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Requiring an explicit agent confirmation step before any write operation is executed, so Claude cannot update records autonomously.
options.B: Configuring the connector to log each write operation with the agent session ID, the specific field updated, and a timestamp.
options.C: Restricting the write scope to fields that are non-clinical in nature, ensuring patient clinical data cannot be modified by Claude.
options.D: Implementing a read-back confirmation step after each write to verify the PRM received the update correctly.
options.E: Encrypting all data transmitted between Claude and the PRM connector to protect patient information in transit.

items.question:
An operations director at a specialty insurance broker is designing a Claude-assisted workflow for producing renewal packs for commercial clients. The workflow is 80% designed: data extraction from the policy management system, Claude-assisted draft generation, and a distribution step are all defined. The director is now designing the resilience layer before finalising the workflow for rollout.

What should the director specify FIRST in the resilience layer?

options.A: The maximum acceptable queue depth before Claude-generated drafts are considered at risk of breaching SLAs.
options.B: A documented manual procedure for draft production that account handlers can execute without Claude when the service is unavailable.
options.C: An automated monitoring alert that notifies the operations team when Claude's average response time exceeds 60 seconds.
options.D: A secondary Claude deployment on an alternative API key to absorb traffic if the primary account reaches its rate limit.

items.question:
A data analyst at a media agency exports campaign performance data from an ad platform and uploads it to Claude for trend analysis. The exported file contains data from multiple clients in the same spreadsheet. Claude's analysis references all clients' data in its summary.

What is the PRIMARY data management error in this workflow?

options.A: The analyst should have used a connector to the ad platform rather than an exported file.
options.B: The multi-client data file was uploaded without separating clients, causing Claude to produce a commingled analysis that violates client data segregation.
options.C: Claude cannot reliably distinguish between multiple clients in a single spreadsheet without explicit labelling of each row.
options.D: The ad platform export should have been reviewed by the account director before upload to confirm data accuracy.

items.question:
A campaign operations manager at a non-profit uses Claude to generate donation acknowledgement emails for 10,000 supporters after a major fundraising campaign. The proposed workflow generates all 10,000 emails and triggers bulk email delivery immediately after generation with no intermediate review step.

What is the MOST important checkpoint to add before delivery?

options.A: A word-count check to confirm each email meets the minimum length standard before delivery.
options.B: A sample review of 10–20 generated emails to verify accuracy of personalisation and donor details before triggering bulk send.
options.C: An automated subject-line scan to check for prohibited words that may trigger spam filters.
options.D: A delivery rate limiter that sends 500 emails per hour rather than all 10,000 simultaneously.

items.question:
A support team lead at a SaaS company configures two paths for their Claude-assisted ticket triage:

**Path 1:** Tickets involving billing disputes above £500 are automatically routed to the billing specialist team.
**Path 2:** When Claude's service is unavailable, all tickets are queued and handled manually by support agents.

Which statement CORRECTLY describes the relationship between these two paths?

options.A: Both paths are escalation paths, because both route work away from Claude to a human resource.
options.B: Path 1 is an escalation path triggered by case characteristics; Path 2 is a fallback path triggered by system unavailability.
options.C: Path 1 is a fallback path; Path 2 is an escalation path triggered when volume exceeds Claude's capacity.
options.D: Both paths are fallback paths, because both activate when the standard workflow cannot proceed.

items.question:
An HR system administrator at a bank configures Claude to generate termination letters based on employee records. A manager proposes that when the termination reason is 'voluntary resignation' and no performance issues are flagged, the letter should be emailed to the employee automatically without any HR review.

What is the PRIMARY concern with this proposal?

options.A: Claude may generate letters with inconsistent tone across different voluntary resignation cases.
options.B: Termination letters are employment-consequential documents; auto-sending without HR review creates STP on a document that may require legal accuracy and could be subject to challenge.
options.C: The proposal would require integration with the email system, which adds technical complexity to the workflow.
options.D: Employees who receive AI-generated termination letters may react negatively if they discover the process was automated.

items.question:
A solutions architect at a wealth management firm is configuring a Claude connector to the firm's portfolio management system (PMS). The connector is intended to help relationship managers quickly retrieve client portfolio summaries during client calls. The architect proposes granting the connector access to all client records and all portfolio data fields in the PMS.

What design principle does this configuration violate?

options.A: Resilience — a single connector with broad access is a single point of failure if the PMS connection is lost.
options.B: Least privilege — the connector should be granted access only to the data fields and client records necessary for the specific use case, not all available data.
options.C: Auditability — broad access makes it harder to trace which data was accessed for each client conversation.
options.D: Segregation of duties — relationship managers and back-office staff should not use the same data connector.

items.question:
A product owner at a fintech company is mapping a loan application workflow. Claude assists with document extraction, credit analysis, and draft decision letters. The product owner asks which step MUST have a mandatory human review before proceeding.

Which answer is MOST accurate?

options.A: Document extraction — because errors in extracted data propagate to all downstream steps.
options.B: Credit analysis — because the model's reasoning is complex and requires actuarial oversight.
options.C: The credit decision itself — because lending decisions affecting a consumer's access to credit are consequential decisions that require human accountability.
options.D: Draft decision letters — because external communications to applicants must be reviewed before sending.

items.question:
General counsel at a large pharmaceutical company is asked by the head of AI operations: 'If we receive a discovery request related to an AI-assisted regulatory submission, what records do we need to be able to produce?' The general counsel's answer defines the minimum audit trail the AI workflow must generate.

Which answer MOST completely identifies the required records?

options.A: The final submitted document and the name of the signatory.
options.B: The AI-generated draft, the reviewer's edits or confirmation of no changes, the approver's identity and timestamp, and the prompt or task description used to generate the draft.
options.C: The AI-generated draft and the email chain approving it for submission.
options.D: The final submitted document and a written declaration from the responsible officer that the content is accurate.

items.question:
A finance controller at a mid-size retailer uses Claude to convert unstructured supplier invoices into a structured format for entry into the accounts payable system. Claude extracts: vendor name, invoice number, line items, VAT amount, and total. Before the finance team manually enters this data into the AP system, the controller learns that the AP system uses a different VAT calculation convention than the invoices Claude is processing.

What should the controller do BEFORE resuming the workflow?

options.A: Instruct Claude to apply the AP system's VAT convention in its extraction output, updating the prompt to account for the difference.
options.B: Add a review step where the AP clerk verifies the VAT figures against the original invoices before AP entry, to catch any convention mismatch.
options.C: Run a reconciliation of all invoices processed to date to determine whether any VAT amounts entered into the AP system are incorrect.
options.D: Suspend the workflow and assess whether Claude's extraction output is compatible with the AP system's convention before continuing.

items.question:
A case manager at a government benefits agency uses Claude in multi-turn conversations to gather and verify applicant information for benefit claims. When a Claude session is unexpectedly terminated mid-conversation, the case manager must restart with a new session and re-gather information the applicant has already provided.

What workflow feature would MOST directly address this resilience gap?

options.A: Increase the session timeout limit so Claude's context window remains active for longer between interactions.
options.B: Configure Claude to summarise gathered applicant information to a persistent case record at defined intervals during the conversation, so progress is preserved regardless of session state.
options.C: Train case managers to save a copy of the conversation transcript at regular intervals during long cases.
options.D: Redesign the workflow to collect all applicant information in a single session rather than across multiple turns.

items.question:
A regional director at a commercial real estate firm uses Claude to draft letters of intent (LOIs) for property acquisitions. The current workflow: Claude generates the LOI based on deal parameters; an associate reviews it; the LOI is sent to the seller. The regional director proposes removing the associate review to reduce the typical 2-day turnaround to same-day.

A senior partner objects, citing a case where an associate's review caught an LOI that used the wrong purchase price due to a conversion error in the deal parameters.

What is the MOST accurate assessment of the regional director's proposal?

options.A: The proposal is justified: a 2-day review delay is competitively disadvantageous in a fast-moving market, and a single historical error is insufficient basis for maintaining the review step.
options.B: The proposal should be partially adopted: automate the review for standard LOIs and retain manual review only for LOIs above a defined transaction value.
options.C: The proposal is not justified: an LOI creates a preliminary commitment to deal terms; removing the review step creates STP on an external legal instrument where errors could be commercially binding.
options.D: The proposal is justified if the deal parameter input step is enhanced with a validation check to prevent conversion errors before Claude generates the LOI.

items.question:
A head of operations at an insurance company is comparing two Claude-assisted workflows:

**Workflow X:** 5,000 routine claim acknowledgement emails per day (no coverage determination, purely administrative confirmation).
**Workflow Y:** 30 complex liability assessments per day (determining coverage position for disputed claims).

The head of operations proposes applying the same human review model to both: 100% human review before any output is sent or actioned.

A business analyst argues this is inefficient for Workflow X and underserved for Workflow Y.

What review design would MOST appropriately serve both workflows?

options.A: Apply a 5% random sample review to Workflow X and 100% human review to Workflow Y, calibrated by the stakes and reversibility of each output type.
options.B: Apply 100% review to both, as the analyst's argument prioritises efficiency over governance.
options.C: Apply 100% review to Workflow X (high volume requires more oversight) and 50% review to Workflow Y (low volume means fewer total reviews).
options.D: Apply automated quality checks to both workflows and remove human review from both, as Claude's accuracy is sufficient for insurance operations.

items.question:
A credit analyst at a bank uses a Claude connector to pull current interest rate reference data from the bank's treasury system. During a period of system maintenance, the treasury system returns cached rate data that is 5 days old. Claude uses this data to draft loan pricing sheets, which are reviewed by a pricing officer and approved without either party noticing the stale rates.

What does this incident PRIMARILY reveal about the workflow design?

options.A: The connector should be designed to include the data timestamp in Claude's output, so the pricing officer can verify the currency of the reference data before approving the pricing sheet.
options.B: The pricing officer failed in their review duty and should have independently verified the rates before approval.
options.C: The treasury system's maintenance window should be scheduled outside business hours to avoid affecting loan pricing workflows.
options.D: Claude should be prompted to query whether the data it has received is current before producing a pricing output.

items.question:
A financial advice operations lead is designing a Claude-assisted workflow to help junior advisers draft client suitability reports for investment recommendations. The workflow design so far: (1) Claude analyses the client's risk profile, investment objectives, and product features; (2) Claude drafts a suitability narrative; (3) the junior adviser reviews the narrative. A compliance manager reviews the design and points out that a regulated firm cannot rely on a junior adviser's unsupervised review as the final approval step for a suitability report.

What should the operations lead specify NEXT to address the compliance manager's concern?

options.A: Replace Claude with a rule-based engine for suitability analysis, which is easier to audit than an LLM.
options.B: Add a senior adviser or compliance officer approval step between the junior adviser's review and the report being sent to the client, with the approver confirming the suitability rationale.
options.C: Instruct Claude to include a disclaimer in the suitability narrative stating that the report has been produced with AI assistance.
options.D: Require the junior adviser to document their specific comments or edits before the report advances, to create a record of their review.

items.question: A chief operations officer at a regulated consumer credit firm is reviewing a Claude-assisted workflow for processing credit limit increase requests. The workflow must satisfy two requirements: (1) every decision must be traceable to a named human authoriser; (2) the firm must be able to process requests even if Claude is unavailable for up to 8 hours. Which TWO design features MOST directly address both requirements? (Choose TWO)

options.A: A mandatory human approval step where a named credit officer reviews Claude's analysis and records their approval decision before the credit limit is updated.
options.B: A real-time dashboard showing Claude's processing queue, enabling managers to monitor throughput during normal operations.
options.C: A documented manual credit assessment procedure, trained across the credit officer team, that can be activated when Claude is unavailable.
options.D: An automated rollback mechanism that reverses any credit limit changes made while Claude was unavailable, once Claude service is restored.
options.E: A secondary Claude project configured with the same system prompt, accessible to a different team member if the primary user's account is restricted.

items.question:
A policy analyst at a government agency uses Claude to draft responses to citizen enquiries about benefit entitlements. A quality review found that 8% of Claude's drafts contain inaccurate entitlement calculations. The agency head proposes fixing this by routing all responses through three levels of review: analyst, supervisor, and legal officer — before sending.

A process engineer argues this three-level review is disproportionate and will create a 5-day response time, compared to the agency's 3-day SLA.

What is the BEST resolution?

options.A: Accept the three-level review: for government benefit responses, thoroughness is more important than SLA compliance.
options.B: Eliminate the review step and fix the 8% error rate by refining Claude's prompt to include the current entitlement calculation rules.
options.C: Apply risk stratification: route complex or high-value entitlement cases through all three review levels; route straightforward cases through analyst review only after prompt refinement to reduce the 8% error rate.
options.D: Reduce the SLA to 5 days to accommodate the three-level review without changing the workflow structure.

items.question:
A head of compliance at an asset management firm learns that the firm's Claude-assisted trade reconciliation workflow has been updated three times in the past quarter — the system prompt, the escalation criteria, and the output format all changed. A regulatory enquiry asks the firm to explain how a specific reconciliation exception from six weeks ago was handled.

What audit record does the firm need to answer this question completely?

options.A: The reconciliation exception report from six weeks ago and the email approving the exception resolution.
options.B: The current system prompt and escalation criteria, plus the exception report and resolution approval.
options.C: The system prompt, escalation criteria, and output format that were active six weeks ago, together with the exception report and the identity and timestamp of the person who reviewed and resolved the exception.
options.D: The log of all three workflow updates showing what changed and when, plus the final exception report.

items.question: A clinical systems director at a large hospital network is designing a Claude-assisted workflow for generating medication reconciliation reports at patient admission. The reports list discrepancies between the patient's reported home medications and active hospital prescriptions. Which TWO design controls are MOST critical for patient safety in this workflow? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Requiring a pharmacist or prescribing clinician to review and sign off on each reconciliation report before any discrepancy is acted upon.
options.B: Configuring Claude to flag cases where the source data (reported medications vs. prescription list) appears incomplete or contradictory, routing these to the pharmacist as priority cases.
options.C: Storing each reconciliation report in the EHR with a timestamp and the patient's admission ID, enabling retrospective audit of reconciliation decisions.
options.D: Using a read-only connector to the hospital's pharmacy system so Claude can access active prescriptions directly rather than relying on manually entered data.
options.E: Sending the reconciliation report to the patient so they can confirm the accuracy of their reported home medication list.
